fixture.name: Day Chart Fixture
fixture.note: Synthetic. Paris, 21 June 1990, midday clock time. Sun in the 10th, well above the horizon: an unambiguous day chart. Anchors the sect unit test. Note clock noon in CEST is ~1.8h before solar noon, so the Sun is near but not on the MC.

meta.ephemeris: astronomy-engine (Don Cross), tropical zodiac, mean lunar node

foundation.chartThesis: A day chart with the Sun leading and the chart ruler, Mercury, in domicile in the 10th makes public work, decisions, and visibility the primary organizing arena of your life. The identity (Sun), needs (Moon), and mind (Mercury) cluster in Gemini in the 10th, so reputation, output, and the constant exchange of information become the place where you calibrate who you are. The stabilizers and stressors of the chart all feed into that: Jupiter (benefic of sect) lifts you through allies and networks, while Mars (contrary to sect) puts pressure on shared resources, risk, and control themes.
foundation.centralTension: The most important push-pull is between bold, high-stakes action and the need to protect trust, stability, and continuity with other people. Mars in Aries in the 8th (domicile, contrary to sect) wants decisive moves around shared money, commitments, and power dynamics, while Jupiter in Cancer in the 11th (exalted, in sect) wants growth through belonging, goodwill, and protective alliances, and Saturn in Capricorn in the 5th (domicile, in sect) insists on earned results and controlled exposure. This shows up as a recurring question: when do you act fast and take the risk, and when do you slow down to preserve relationships, reputation, and the long game.
foundation.dominantPattern: A double emphasis on Gemini/10th and Capricorn/5th creates a repeatable loop: you produce and communicate in public, then you return to a private standard of craft, rigor, and self-judgment about what you made. You tend to solve problems by thinking, naming, and iterating quickly (Mercury in Gemini 10th; Moon conjunct Mercury), but you evaluate the result through long timelines and high internal thresholds (Saturn in Capricorn 5th, retrograde, domicile). This makes you capable of sustained excellence, but it also makes it easy to keep moving the finish line, especially around creative output and recognition.

sectionGuidance.mind: Make Mercury the centerpiece: describe how you process, decide, and speak when it is fast and exposed (10th), and how the Mercury–Mars sextile turns thinking into decisive action, including the edge it gives in negotiation and the impatience it can create.
sectionGuidance.focus: Use the Lots and nodes to define the developmental aim: Spirit in Virgo 1st as agency through method and self-definition; Fortune in Leo 12th as circumstance tied to retreat/behind-the-scenes visibility; North Node in Aquarius 6th as growth through systems, routines, and service that protect your nervous system from 10th-house overexposure.
sectionGuidance.money: Tie money to the 2nd ruler Venus in domicile in the 9th: show how earnings grow through expertise, education, publishing, travel, or a defined aesthetic and ethical stance, and add the 8th-house Mars as the pressure point around shared money, debt, and risk.
sectionGuidance.triad: Differentiate Sun, Moon, and Ascendant ruler without overlap: Sun in Gemini 10th as recognition-purpose; Moon in Gemini 10th as regulation-through-communication; Mercury as the decisive instrument and personal engine because it rules the 1st and 10th in domicile.
sectionGuidance.career: Anchor career in 10th ruler Mercury in domicile with Sun/Moon there: identify the specific kinds of roles where you are seen for communication, synthesis, and responsiveness, and show how Jupiter 11th brings opportunities through patrons, teams, and audiences.
sectionGuidance.family: Read home and origin through the 4th ruler Jupiter in the 11th: family as a network system (chosen and blood), moves shaped by community, and the need for a supportive social ecosystem to feel rooted rather than a purely private retreat.
sectionGuidance.overview: Establish the locomotive shape and the Gemini/10th + Capricorn/5th double-center as the life rhythm: public output and communication followed by private refinement, with alliances as the amplifier (Jupiter 11th).
sectionGuidance.discoveries: Focus on the main failure modes that teach you: Mars square Neptune and Jupiter opposite Neptune as the pattern of projection, porous boundaries, or wishful scaling, and how you learn to replace belief with verification without losing momentum.
sectionGuidance.superpowers: Name three usable strengths with proof: Mercury in domicile 10th for clarity and adaptability in public; Venus trine Saturn (orb 2.1 applying) for durable taste and disciplined craft; Jupiter trine Pluto (orb 1.9 applying) for influence through research-level depth and persuasive framing.
sectionGuidance.relationships: Read partnership through the 7th ruler Jupiter in Cancer 11th: partners via friends/groups, loyalty and protection as the bonding style, and bring in Chiron in the 7th as the tender spot around being relied upon or seen as 'safe' without being fully known.

paradoxes.title: Public mind, private luck
paradoxes.tension: You can think on your feet in front of other people and feel most regulated when there is dialogue, messaging, and real-time feedback. You also keep getting results through quiet channels you cannot fully manage: a closed-door ally, an unadvertised opportunity, a period of retreat that changes your trajectory. You notice the irony that the more you chase certainty through visibility, the more noise you attract, and the less the helpful, hidden support can find you. You oscillate between proving yourself loudly and disappearing to restore your edge.
paradoxes.invitation: Treat privacy as an active tool, not a failure of confidence. You do best when you choose one or two visible arenas and keep the rest intentionally unbroadcast. When you protect recovery time and selective access, your reputation stays sharp and your timing improves, with real openings arriving.

paradoxes.title: Loyal circles, sharp cuts
paradoxes.tension: You want to build goodwill and belong to a steady circle that protects its own. You also have a streak that moves fast when stakes feel personal: you press for clarity, you demand clean terms, and you would rather end an entanglement than live with ambiguity. This can confuse people who know you as generous and team-minded, because you can switch from warm inclusion to decisive separation in a single conversation. You see it most around shared money, shared responsibility, or any situation where trust and leverage are intertwined.
paradoxes.invitation: Let your loyalty include rules. Name the terms early, before heat rises, and you will not need to escalate to get honesty. When you practise firm agreements as an act of care, you keep your alliances and your autonomy at the same time, with less collateral damage.

paradoxes.title: Sweet values, expensive hope
paradoxes.tension: You have real taste and you know what quality feels like in your body. You can be steady about what you value, and you prefer investments that grow slowly and hold. Yet help and opportunity can arrive wrapped in optimism that asks you to move faster than your standards: a group plan that sounds perfect, a generous promise that is light on details, a vision that blurs the actual cost. You can find yourself paying for someone else’s dream with your time, your money, or your credibility, then cleaning up quietly afterward.
paradoxes.invitation: Keep the sweetness and add verification. Ask for numbers, dates, and accountability before you commit resources or name a partnership publicly. When you hold the dream to a practical timeline, you still get to say yes, but on terms that protect your future, with trust earned in steps.

actions.action: Ask one well-placed friend for a single introduction you have been avoiding.

actions.why: Clarity activates support and prevents others from guessing wrong.
actions.action: Send three short messages that name what you can offer and what you want next.

actions.why: Your momentum builds when your work is witnessed and reinforced.
actions.action: Join one working group for the next 30 days and show up once a week.

growingEdge.text: You are pulled toward a working life where consistency matters more than intensity. You can do brilliant bursts, but you grow when you build repeatable systems that protect your energy, time, and attention. You can check this by watching what happens when your week has no routine: your output may still be high, but your body feels wired, and small tasks start to feel strangely heavy. The uncomfortable part is choosing constraints on purpose, especially when you could keep improvising. The payoff is real: simple structures turn your skill into something dependable, and they reduce the need to prove yourself in public every day.
growingEdge.title: Systems Over Spark

actions.why: A small routine stabilises your nervous system and reduces last-minute surges.
actions.action: Choose one daily minimum for the next seven days: 30 minutes of focused maintenance work at the same time each day.

actions.why: External structure prevents mental churn and frees attention for higher-level thinking.
actions.action: Make a one-page checklist for a task you repeat and use it once this week.

actions.why: You learn to value steady contribution without overextending for recognition.
actions.action: Do one act of service that is unglamorous and measurable, then stop.

chronicPattern.text: When money, trust, or power is shared, you move fast and sharp. You can cut through denial, spot leverage, and push a decision to the table before others are ready. You can check this by how quickly your body tightens when someone is vague about a promise, a payment, or a timeline. The cost is that urgency can turn into pressure, and pressure can turn into a fight you did not mean to start. You are also prone to acting on a compelling story before every detail is verified, especially when you want to protect someone or prove you can handle it. This pattern does not disappear. It becomes manageable when you slow the first move.
chronicPattern.title: High-Stakes Heat

actions.why: Precision cools reactivity and prevents later resentment.
actions.action: Before any shared-money decision this week, write a two-line definition of the deal: who owes what, by when, and what happens if it fails.

actions.why: You keep your edge without escalating the stakes.
actions.action: Delay one impulsive message by 20 minutes and reread it for threat, blame, or hidden ultimatum.

actions.why: Verification stops you from paying for optimism with your peace.
actions.action: Pick one situation where you feel responsible for saving the outcome and ask one direct fact-check question.

relationships.howYouLove: You love through loyalty in public and tenderness in private. You feel secure when your partner is kind to your friendships, respects your ambitions, and can show up as a steady ally instead of a rival. You give by making introductions, advocating, sharing opportunities, and protecting your partner’s name when they are not in the room. What attracts you is competence with warmth: someone who can nurture, host, and build belonging, not just someone who is exciting. What you say you want is “easy” and “low-drama,” but what actually pulls you in is a person with a real life, real responsibilities, and a clear moral center you can trust when pressure hits.
relationships.theChallenge: You have a repeat pattern of moving quickly into deep entanglement, then discovering you were negotiating two different realities. It can start with big promises, shared plans, or an intense feeling of being chosen, and then turns into friction around money, timing, sexual expectations, or who holds the power in a crisis. You are direct, and you can argue like a professional, but you can also overestimate how much clarity you have when you are emotionally invested. When trust wobbles, you go into investigation mode, and the relationship starts to feel like a case to solve instead of a place to rest.
relationships.whatPartnershipAsks: Partnership asks you to treat intimacy as a long-term ecosystem, not a high-stakes sprint. You grow when you let love be supported by community, shared values, and visible agreements, rather than private tests of loyalty. You are here to practice saying what you need before you are at the breaking point, and to make room for repair without keeping score. You also do better when you separate shared resources from shared emotions, so neither becomes a weapon. The more you build routines that protect your body and your workload, the less you ask a partner to regulate you.

venus_trine_saturn.growth: Treating the ease as a resource to be invested rather than a comfort to rest in.
venus_trine_saturn.dynamic: Venus and Saturn. Venus is attraction, pleasure, taste, and the capacity to draw people in. Saturn is structure, limit, duration, and the discipline that makes things last. Two functions in signs of the same element flow into each other without resistance. What they do together comes easily, often so easily that it goes unnoticed and undervalued.
venus_trine_saturn.tension: Complacency. The gift is taken for granted, left undeveloped, or used as an excuse to avoid harder things.
venus_trine_saturn.behavior: Effortless talent. The two functions combine naturally and reliably.

mars_square_jupiter.growth: Accepting that the tension is permanent and building something out of it rather than trying to resolve it.
mars_square_jupiter.dynamic: Mars and Jupiter. Mars is drive, assertion, and the capacity to cut through and go after something. Jupiter is expansion, confidence, generosity, and the sense that more is possible. Two functions in signs that share a mode but not an element push against each other. Neither yields easily, so the pressure is constant and productive: this is where effort is forced and skill is built.
mars_square_jupiter.tension: Recurring conflict, frustration, and the sense of being pulled two ways at once.
mars_square_jupiter.behavior: Hard-won competence. The friction has been turned into a driving engine.

mercury_sextile_mars.growth: Deliberately using the connection rather than waiting for it to act on its own.
mercury_sextile_mars.dynamic: Mercury and Mars. Mercury is how a person thinks, learns, decides and makes themselves understood. Mars is drive, assertion, and the capacity to cut through and go after something. Two functions in compatible signs support each other when asked. The connection is friendly and productive but not automatic: it is an opportunity rather than a given.
mercury_sextile_mars.tension: Underused. The help is available but not taken, so the opportunity goes quiet.
mercury_sextile_mars.behavior: The two cooperate readily and produce practical results with modest effort.

moon_conjunction_mercury.growth: Learning to feel which of the two is speaking, and to give each its turn.
moon_conjunction_mercury.dynamic: Moon and Mercury. The Moon is the body, the habits, and what makes someone feel safe. Mercury is how a person thinks, learns, decides and makes themselves understood. Two functions occupy the same place and act as one. Neither can be used without engaging the other, so their natures blend, for better or worse depending on how compatible they are.
moon_conjunction_mercury.tension: The two cannot be separated, so the difficulty of one contaminates the other and there is no clean way to use either alone.
moon_conjunction_mercury.behavior: The two work as a single combined strength, each amplifying the other.

jupiter_opposition_saturn.growth: Owning both ends instead of projecting one, and finding the position between them.
jupiter_opposition_saturn.dynamic: Jupiter and Saturn. Jupiter is expansion, confidence, generosity, and the sense that more is possible. Saturn is structure, limit, duration, and the discipline that makes things last. Two functions in opposite signs pull in opposite directions and can see each other clearly. The tension is external and relational: it tends to play out between the person and someone else, or as a swing between two extremes.
jupiter_opposition_saturn.tension: Polarisation. The person identifies with one side and meets the other in someone else, usually as conflict.
jupiter_opposition_saturn.behavior: Balance and perspective. Each side tempers the other and the person can hold both.

personalPlanets.sun: The Sun is the centre of identity and the sense of what one is for. Gemini is quick, curious, verbal, and interested in everything at once. The 10th is vocation, reputation, and what one is known for doing.
personalPlanets.mars: Mars is drive, assertion, and the capacity to cut through and go after something. Aries acts first, directly and fast, and sorts things out afterward. The 8th is shared resources, loss, inheritance, and what is not one's own.
personalPlanets.moon: The Moon is the body, the habits, and what makes someone feel safe. Gemini is quick, curious, verbal, and interested in everything at once. The 10th is vocation, reputation, and what one is known for doing.
personalPlanets.pluto: Pluto is intensity, power, and transformation through what cannot be avoided. Scorpio goes deep, holds on, and does not do anything by halves. The 3rd is the near world: siblings, neighbours, daily talk, and learning.
personalPlanets.venus: Venus is attraction, pleasure, taste, and the capacity to draw people in. Taurus is steady, sensual, slow to start and slower to stop. The 9th is the far world: belief, higher learning, travel, and meaning.
personalPlanets.chiron: Chiron marks a wound that becomes a source of skill and understanding for others. Pisces feels everything, blurs boundaries, and gives more than it keeps. The 7th is the other: partners, spouses, open rivals, and one-to-one bonds.
personalPlanets.saturn: Saturn is structure, limit, duration, and the discipline that makes things last. Capricorn is disciplined, ambitious, and plays the long game. The 5th is pleasure, creativity, children, and what one does for its own sake.
personalPlanets.uranus: Uranus is disruption, independence, and the sudden break from what was expected. Capricorn is disciplined, ambitious, and plays the long game. The 5th is pleasure, creativity, children, and what one does for its own sake.
personalPlanets.jupiter: Jupiter is expansion, confidence, generosity, and the sense that more is possible. Cancer protects, remembers, and holds close what it cares about. The 11th is allies, friends, groups, and hopes shared with others.
personalPlanets.mercury: Mercury is how a person thinks, learns, decides and makes themselves understood. Gemini is quick, curious, verbal, and interested in everything at once. The 10th is vocation, reputation, and what one is known for doing.
personalPlanets.neptune: Neptune is dissolution, longing, imagination, and the blurring of hard edges. Capricorn is disciplined, ambitious, and plays the long game. The 5th is pleasure, creativity, children, and what one does for its own sake.
personalPlanets.north_node: The North Node is the direction of growth: unfamiliar, uncomfortable, and worth it. Aquarius stands apart, thinks in systems, and cares about the group. The 6th is work, routine, health, and what must be maintained.
personalPlanets.south_node: The South Node is the default: what comes easily and what gets overused. Leo is warm, proud, generous, and needs to be seen doing it. The 12th is what is hidden: solitude, sorrow, secrets, and self-undoing.
